meta.title: Finnish C1 Advanced
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Finnish → English (see the Finnish, recall the meaning) and English → Finnish (see an English meaning, recall the Finnish). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words of Finnish for an advanced learner, aligned to C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognise implicit meaning' — a learner here is able to express ideas fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions, to use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes, and to produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Finnish has an examination graded to these levels (the National Certificates of Language Proficiency, YKI), but no graded word list for it was found published, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 186 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — philosophy and ethics, religion and the inner life, scholarly Finnish, government, diplomacy and the constitution, the economy and development, medicine and the body, law and rights, language and literature, the shades of feeling and judgement, the abstract nouns and adjectives of formal prose, and the literary connectors and adverbs — and the other 1314 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Finnish, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case of a noun and every form of a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Verbs are given as Finnish dictionaries give them, in the first infinitive (syödä "to eat", puhua "to speak"). The 852 nouns show their plural, their genitive, their partitive and their plural partitive, the forms consonant gradation and stem changes make hard to guess (käsi, kädet, käden, kättä, käsiä), and behind the All forms fold every case in both numbers; the 251 verbs show their "I" and "he, she" forms, their past and their perfect (syödä: syön, syö, söi, on syönyt), and behind the fold the present, the negative, the past, the perfect, the conditional and the imperative by person, and the passive. The Finnish Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and their sounds. Real example sentences come with 1246 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 928 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
